name: Urhobo
notes: Standard Urhobo (Agbarho dialect, the variety used for writing per Aziza 2007) Latin orthography, developed by the Urhobo Studies Association and formally adopted at its 2008 workshop building on Aziza's phonological description; Omniglot's alphabet chart and Lord's Prayer sample text corroborate the letter inventory. Seven-vowel harmony system /i e ɛ a o ɔ u/ with a full parallel set of nasalized vowels /ĩ ẽ ɛ̃ ã õ ɔ̃ ũ/, each nasal vowel a single nucleus rather than oral-vowel-plus-nasal-consonant (AGENTS.md test 2); ⟨ẹ⟩ and ⟨ọ⟩ mark the open-mid vowels /ɛ/ /ɔ/ distinct from ⟨e⟩ /e/ and ⟨o⟩ /o/ (the same underdotted-vowel convention as neighbouring Cross River/Edoid languages, cf. efi.json). ⟨gb⟩ and ⟨kp⟩ spell the single labial-velar stops /ɡb/ /kp/, ⟨gh⟩ the velar fricative /ɣ/, ⟨ny⟩ the palatal nasal /ɲ/. ⟨rh⟩ spells a voiceless/breathy alveolar tap [ɾ̥], contrasting with plain ⟨r⟩ /ɾ/ (test 3: without a dedicated ⟨rh⟩ key, ⟨r⟩+⟨h⟩ would wrongly read as a tap followed by a separate glottal fricative). ⟨v⟩ is the bilabial approximant /β̞/, one of the five oral consonants (β̞, ɾ, l, j, w) cited as having nasal allophones before nasal vowels. Smoke-tested against the Omniglot Lord's Prayer excerpt: ⟨Ọ da ta kẹ ayen⟩ 'And he said unto them' — ⟨Ọ⟩ [ɔ] '(s)he', ⟨da⟩ [da] 'came/did', ⟨ta⟩ [ta] 'say/speak', ⟨kẹ⟩ [kɛ] 'to/that', ⟨ayen⟩ [ajen] 'them'; ⟨Ovwan⟩ [ɔvwan] 'we/our' and ⟨ẹrhovwo⟩ [ɛɾ̥ɔvwo] 'heaven' both resolve through the mapped graphemes, with ⟨ẹrhovwo⟩ confirming the ⟨rh⟩ breathy-tap digraph. Urhobo has two tones (high, low, with derived rising/falling contours) and no lexical word stress; the acute accent marks high tone in careful orthography but is frequently omitted in ordinary text, so tone is left unencoded here, a documented exemption distinct from stress (docs/quality_tiers.md).
